description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Research for Decision Makers (RDM) activity will support implementation research on priority health areas, provide advisory services to the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) to guide health policy and strategy formulation, and build health-sector research capacity. USAID will also benefit through programmatic guidance from the findings of RDM research. With FY 2021 funds, RDM will continue the implementation of research studies on family planning, maternal and newborn health, and nutrition. RDM will also undertake secondary analysis of recent national health survey data to develop programmatic and policy guidance on key priority health issues. RDM will disseminate the results of the studies and analyses through various channels, which will provide the evidence needed to inform policy and programmatic decision-making by key stakeholders. RDM will collaborate in the implementation of the 2021-22 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey through technical guidance on data analysis on causes of under five deaths and dissemination of preliminary findings. Through RDM, USAID will build local research capacity and expand the evidence base to inform future public health policies in Bangladesh. By assisting the GoB and USAID to translate evidence into policy, RDM will contribute to reducing child and maternal mortality, fertility rates, and tuberculosis incidence rate, while improving the nutritional status of children.This activity will support the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two and the U.S. Government mission objective of improved health status in Bangladesh.
